blocks.text: Condo buildings in Vancouver Heights

TOP FLAG — THE NAME LIES, AND THE MAP HAS THREE TRAPS. Vancouver Heights is in the City of Burnaby (North Burnaby, on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine) — not the City of Vancouver, despite the name. This pass verified 4 apartment-condo buildings by name on building-directory plus listing evidence; three more named buildings (The Mondeo, Verdi, Carleton Terrace) rest on listing evidence only and are carried not verified, not counted. Checked and out-of-area: Burnaby Hospital is at 3935 Kincaid St, south across the city — not in-area.
The Sienna — 3939 Hastings Street

A 22-unit strata building: the building directory records it built in 1998, with bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" and amenities of air conditioning, central air, garden and private yard — the rental-restriction element of that directory line is void since November 24, 2022. Current listings record the subdivision name "The Sienna," Area Minor Vancouver Heights, Apartment/Condo form and a 1998 build year, consistent with the directory. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus name-verifying current listings. Counted: 1.
The Carleton (listing subdivision name "Carleton") — 4223 Hastings Street

No standalone directory FAQ page for the building was surfaced this pass — the directory evidence is the directory site's own building records for the address, stated as such. No rental, pet or age restriction is stated for it in the sources checked — not confirmed per the Form B. Counted: 1.
Heritage Green — 3978 Albert Street

The building directory records Heritage Green built in 1994 with 28 units, in-suite laundry, and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental-restriction element is void since November 24, 2022; the directory records an active listing at the address, and a unit at 3978 Albert Street is carried in the Vancouver Heights MLS listings index. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus listing evidence at the address. Counted: 1.
Evergreen Place — 3861 Albert Street

The building directory records Evergreen Place built in 1989, with in-suite laundry and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" — the rental-restriction element is void since November 24, 2022 — and records the building's listing and sale history at this address, most recently in October 2025; no unit was actively listed at the check. Unit count: Not confirmed from the sources checked. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry plus the directory's recorded listing history at the address. Counted: 1.
Streets, schools and getting around Vancouver Heights

items.t: Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in North Burnaby, on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine; "Vancouver Heights" is the MLS (GVR board) sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The neighbourhood frame in the 55+ notes is Boundary Road west, Gamma Avenue east, Hastings Street south and Burrard Inlet north. West of Boundary Road is the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) — a different municipality, different sub-area.

Where condo stock concentrates: low-rise strata buildings on Hastings Street itself and one block north on Albert Street. The rest of the sub-area is predominantly detached houses on a sloping, view-oriented hillside — early-to-mid-20th-century homes, post-war bungalows and Vancouver Special-era houses alongside newer rebuilds. Strata product is concentrated on/near Hastings.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings Street through the Heights, linking Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak, with in-area stops including Hythe, Holdom and Kensington. On September 7, 2026, TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving the Heights with peak service every 6–7 minutes and replacing the peak-only 222 bus. There is no SkyTrain station in this sub-area.

Schools and catchments (SD41, Burnaby): two elementary schools sit on Pandora Street inside the sub-area — Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora St) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora St) — and the locator splits the street by address range: 4375 Pandora St → Rosser Elementary / Alpha Secondary; 4715 Pandora St → Confederation Park Elementary / Alpha Secondary.

Parks, recreation and civic: Confederation Park (250 Willingdon Ave), Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre (240 Willingdon Ave) and the McGill Branch of Burnaby Public Library (4595 Albert St) form the west-end civic cluster; Capitol Hill Reservoir Park (229 N Hythe Ave) is listed by the City as a scenic viewpoint park. The City's planned new Confederation Park Community Centre beside the pool and library has been deferred by the City. In August 2026 the Province announced funding for 20 new child-care spaces at Confederation Park Elementary.
Health care: there is no hospital in the sub-area; Burnaby Hospital is at 3935 Kincaid St, south across the city — checked, and out-of-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Vancouver Heights

items.t: The building called "The Heights" is not filed in Vancouver Heights. The Heights (3768 Hastings St, 1998, 37 units) carries this neighbourhood's name, but its own MLS listing record places it under the Willingdon Heights sub-area — it stands on the south side of Hastings at the west edge.
Carleton appears twice, too. Confirm the street address, not just the name, before booking a showing.

One street, two elementary schools, and the "obvious" secondary is not the right one. Pandora Street carries both in-area elementaries, and the SD41 locator splits it by address range: 4375 Pandora St → Rosser Elementary, 4715 Pandora St → Confederation Park Elementary, both feeding Alpha Secondary in the district's results, not Burnaby North Secondary, the school physically located in North Burnaby. Check the school by address rather than by name.
Detached sold briskly while attached barely moved. Price an attached unit against the attached evidence, not the hillside's detached headline. SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

Burnaby replaced both of its governing documents within seven months. The Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) replaced the 1998 OCP, and the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, in effect July 1, 2026) replaced the 1965 zoning bylaw — and the new OCP takes precedence over the older neighbourhood community-plan maps, including for the Hastings corridor's Heights Urban Village. Any Heights document or old listing citing the 1965 bylaw or the 1998 OCP as current is out of date twice over.
The seniors tower stands on a heritage estate. The tower itself opened in 1974 and is rental/care: it anchors the area's seniors services without adding a single buyable unit.
The claim that Brentwood is the nearest enclosed mall is not verified — the Heights' own shopping is the Hastings street-front strip, and no source checked states the mall claim as fact.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Vancouver Heights
Streets, schools and getting around Vancouver Heights

items.t: Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby neighbourhood in northwest Burnaby (North Burnaby), on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its spine; the MLS® sub-area name (GVR board) is "Vancouver Heights." Nearby areas: Capitol Hill (the hilltop portion within/adjacent to this sub-area), Willingdon Heights, Parkcrest, Lochdale, Westridge, Burnaby Heights to the west, and the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise) across Boundary Road.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: it does not form complexes here. No named townhouse complex inside the sub-area was verified, the condos pass, the 55-plus pass or this pass.

Schools (SD41; Ministry-listed names only) — settled chain cited: the SD41 locator run documented for the sample in-area address 4375 Pandora St (locator range 4303–4375 PANDORA ST) returned Rosser Elementary (K–7) / Alpha Secondary (8–12) (SD41 School Locator, run 2026-11-01). Vancouver Heights catchment = Alpha Secondary for that address range. Two SD41 elementary schools sit on Pandora Street inside the sub-area — Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora St) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora St) — and the Capitol Hill sample (4715 Pandora St) returned Confederation Park Elementary / Alpha Secondary, so the two in-area Pandora elementaries split the street by address range while the secondary stays Alpha. Burnaby North Secondary (751 Hammarskjold Drive) is the other secondary school located in North Burnaby — location is not catchment. Catchments for other Heights addresses: Not verified.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings through the Heights (Burrard Station to SFU; at least every 10 minutes at peak, 15 minutes off-peak; stops include Hythe, Holdom and Kensington). On September 7, 2026, TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving Burnaby Heights with peak service every six to seven minutes and replacing the peak-only 222 bus.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Vancouver Heights

items.t: Form B diligence (strata frame): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

SSMUH on house lots: under the R1 SSMUH District, most Heights lots allow 3–6 homes (6 only within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop) and multi-unit product may be stratified — so two otherwise similar houses can be worth very different amounts to builders depending on lot area and the 400 m transit test (the R5/R2 Hastings corridor makes that test live on many lots). Review the Burnaby 2050 OCP land use map and the Heights Urban Village direction before assuming redevelopment or assembly value on Hastings-fronting and near-Hastings properties, because the new OCP takes precedence over older community plan maps.

blocks.text: Vancouver Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

15 condos sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $565,000 (the middle half sold between $491,500 and $976,900), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 95.9% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $790 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $397 a month. 5 townhomes sold in Vancouver Heights with a median price of $835,000, taking a median of 25 days to sell at 98.0% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $794 per square foot, a median year built of 2003 and a median strata fee of $470 a month.
